scope: Maker/library/instrument and root/folder/sample presentation over existing discovery evidence
Contextual search without aggregate sibling-tag inheritance
Per-category browsing and temporary search restoration
Native outline interaction, stale evidence, and plugin-removal regression
Session navigation registry and compatibility boundaries
nonblocking_assessment: The increment is explicitly narrower than the full redesign: it changes presentation, not adapters, storage measurement, historical usage, metadata editing, or removal authority.
Separate physical installations and shared-container product identities remain distinct; proposed/unresolved identities cannot appear as verified products.
Per-instrument matching plus explicit library-only matches prevents a broad library description from inventing installed instrument matches.
Root precedence, distinct equal-name roots, real discovered paths, and flat sample search provide testable folder and breadcrumb semantics.
Browse state and temporary search state are deliberately separate; reset and persistence exclusions are explicit and registry checks are required.

The plan requires runtime native interaction and independent UX review rather than treating a build as proof of hierarchy usability. Full VoiceOver and older-target coverage remain explicitly unverified.
verification_counterexamples: Collapse a library, search for a deeply nested patch, change search text to no matches, then clear: prior browse selection and expansion must return.
Two instruments with identical titles or paths but distinct vendor IDs, and two installations with one product ID, must retain independent row identities.
An Accordion aggregate tag on a library containing an unrelated piano must not make the piano an Accordion result.
Switch categories while search is active, then return and clear it: no search-selected row may overwrite that category's previous browse selection.
Refresh while an instrument is selected and while persistence first assigns observation IDs: reconcile proven identity without jumping to a same-named sibling.
Cached stale child instruments must remain visibly stale in both row and inspector; choosing a group must not inherit a previous leaf's Finder or removal action.
Native runtime validation should inspect accessible row names/disclosure state and actual arrow-key traversal, not merely programmatic expansion.
limitations: Specification critique only; no implementation, builds, or runtime validation performed.
Alternate Claude client is reported unauthenticated by the coordinator; this is an independent Codex review, not cross-client agreement.
No product code or blind holdout criteria were modified or accessed. Only this report was written.
